raw_text:
Money Talk

*   OpenAI's revenue "update" is apparently a $20 billion haircut from earlier whispers; the reported $50 billion annualized figure made AI darlings like Nvidia and Oracle take a dive. Turns out even AI hype has its limits.
*   Oil prices jumped 5% on Middle East tensions and hurricane threats, making Trump's declaration that the US won't attack Iran *before midterms* sound a bit quaint. Spoiler: gas prices are still expected to be above $4 a gallon by Election Day. Oof.
*   The Trump administration is cracking down on foreign worker programs for tech giants like Microsoft and Adobe, citing "multiple active federal investigations." Looks like Big Tech's talent pipeline just got a lot tighter.
*   The NY Fed just dropped a bomb, saying tariffs were entirely to blame for 2.9 percentage points of inflation in 67 categories of everyday goods. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs bosses are gearing up to split a cool $500 million in bonuses. Read the room, guys.
*   Across the pond, the Swiss National Bank cut interest rates by a half-point, sending the franc down against the dollar, while Germany's manufacturing PMI is hitting a four-month high. Europe's economy is giving off some seriously mixed signals.

World Lore

*   The US just slapped former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with new torture charges, effectively escalating the pressure cooker on the ousted authoritarian. Guess the feds decided the drug trafficking charges weren't spicy enough.
*   South Korea is having a moment of geopolitical drama: recalling its ambassador to Ukraine over a North Korean POW dispute (you can't make this up) and simultaneously test-flying its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon. The message to Pyongyang seems pretty clear: "Don't mess with us."
*   Back in Ukraine, Russian strikes continue to be brutal, with a public bus attack killing 30 people and worsening Kyiv's blackouts. A grim reminder of the daily reality on the ground as the world debates the next big thing.
*   In a quiet diplomatic chess move, the EU's diplomatic service (and Canada and Lithuania) just pulled support from a disinformation event, reportedly due to US pressure and "uncomfortable framing." Sounds like some serious behind-the-scenes wrangling over who gets to define truth.
*   Beyond the daily headlines, the IMF chief issued a stark economic warning for 2027, urging leaders to prepare, while reports suggest China's collaborative approach to AI adoption could put it ahead of the US. The future is coming, and it might not be American-made.

Tech Tea

*   OpenAI's $50 billion annualized revenue, while massive, is reportedly $20 billion *less* than previous projections. The market took it personally, with AI darlings sinking. Even the poster child of hype isn't immune to a reality check.
*   Google's Gemini is officially becoming your new AI agent coworker: it can plan, execute tasks, delegate to "subagents," and even gets its own workplace identity and email address. Just wait until it starts sending passive-aggressive calendar invites.
*   Turns out Ben Affleck is a legit AI nerd. He sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year and is now going viral for dropping deep knowledge on neural networks and transformers. Forget Batman, he's Bat-AI-man now.
*   Amazon is finally phasing out its Fire Tablets, replacing them with "Alexa Tablets" that run *actual* Android with full Play Store access. It's a massive pivot from their walled garden approach, and some are speculating it's a blueprint for an Amazon phone. Please, let it be better than the Fire Phone.
*   Anthropic is updating Claude's usage policy to ban "abusive or cruel behavior" towards the AI, alongside the usual no-nos like election interference and weapons development. It's a curious turn to protect the AI itself, but a necessary one as these models get more sophisticated (and potentially sensitive).

Creator Szn

*   Revlon, a true heritage brand, is leaning into its legacy by tapping Teyana Taylor and Megan Moroney for its "Be Unforgettable" campaign. Smart move: in a sea of fleeting trends, sometimes looking to the past is the freshest play.
*   Agencies are going full throttle on AI, with one firm cutting a six-week project down to four *days* using an "AI pressure cooker." While it promises big savings, it also highlights the very real risk of creative burnout. More speed, less sleep, right?
*   Speaking of AI in agencies, clients are reportedly getting cold feet about "rogue" agentic media, with whispers of a mysterious "Hugging Face Incident." Sounds like an untold horror story from the cutting edge of digital advertising.
*   Apple just dropped a deadline on publishers by blocking certain ad tech on Safari, forcing them back to the IAB Tech Lab's Trusted Server. Yet another privacy-first move from Cupertino that's reshaping how digital ads (and content) are served and tracked.
*   The Verge is asking the question on everyone's mind: "Are you ready for everything to look like TikTok?" From Instagram Reels to LinkedIn's vertical video feeds, the short-form, endless-scroll UI has officially conquered every corner of the digital experience. Resistance is futile.

Speed Round

*   Elon Musk admitted some of his Trump posts on X "went too far," showing a rare moment of internet self-reflection.
*   Trump declared anyone using "AI" instead of "Super Intelligence" "THE ENEMY!" — even if the White House uses the former.
*   The US Labor Department announced a record low stretch of unemployment claims, suggesting a surprisingly robust labor market.
*   The Bank of England's rate decision was delayed by two minutes for a VE Day silence, proving even central bankers have moments of solemnity.
*   British defense officials are blocking new windfarms due to fears their spinning blades would interfere with radar systems.
*   New York is accusing TikTok of giving users "placebo" safety features, raising serious questions about platform integrity.
*   Ben Affleck, apparently, is a bona fide AI expert, deep-diving into neural networks after selling his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix.
